analysis:
The supplied units are BASE-side excerpts of CHANGELOG.md (lines 823-1370, release notes for v0.10.2 through v0.10.4 and the tail of the dev-branch lane notes). The patch shows the head adds about 400 lines of v0.10.7 candidate notes, but only a truncated excerpt of that text is supplied. I could not review the new head content beyond the opening upgrade notes (pair update, cluster tensor-parallel wire changes, public Gemma 4/MiMo TP models).

The changelog is documentation, so it changes no executable control directly. I examined the base text for security-relevant claims that the threat model relies on. The SSD prefix-cache notes are relevant to T-041: 30-minute TTL, HMAC-keyed names, a daily write budget and per-checkpoint ownership checks. The add-on hold hardening notes are relevant to TB-012, T-059 and T-060: signer verification before a socket slot is taken, a 10-second request line limit, and non-blocking reads of the FIFO-guarded hold record. The release-lane notes are relevant to T-034 and T-043: Developer ID signing, notarization, and a designated-requirement check before upload. These are historical statements and describe no new behavior in this PR. They do not contradict the threat model, which already describes these controls.

The diff cannot be checked against code in this batch. Open questions for integration: (1) whether the v0.10.7 notes, such as the pair-serving grants and the declared public cluster models, imply any new trust boundary (a Mac-to-Mac cluster/tensor-parallel wire) that the threat model does not cover, and (2) whether the claims about coordinator-side requirements (darkbloom-platform PRs) match the platform-owned policy. No concrete regression or attack surface is evidenced in the supplied lines, so there are no findings, but the head-side cluster content was not visible, so deeper review is warranted.
